--- title: "Internal standards and outliers (3.1–3.7)" --- ::: {.cell} ::: The internal standards (IS) are the backbone of the quality control: they are added in the same amount to every sample, so their peak areas should be the same everywhere. Page 3 of the app, **Quality control and normalization**, first checks them: which ones fail, which samples are outliers, and how stable they are over the run. ## 3.1 Internal standards All internal standards with their retention time, m/z, the RSD% of their raw peak areas over all samples, and the number of samples where they were not found (zero). **Failed** IS are red. In the app, select a row (or use the arrow keys ↑ / ↓) to show that IS in 3.4 and 3.5. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip} - **A low RSD%** (e.g. below 20–30%) means the IS was measured consistently; a high RSD% points to drift, matrix effects or injection problems, which normalization should correct. - **Zero values** are samples where the IS was not found. ::: ## 3.2 Failed internal standards An IS **fails** when more than 10% of the samples have a zero value: it cannot be trusted to normalize the others. Failed IS are removed before normalization. Here 2 of 22 internal standards failed. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## 3.3 Outlier samples A sample is an **outlier** when more than 20% of the internal standards deviate by more than 3 standard deviations from their mean (in log scale): something went wrong with the whole sample, e.g. a wrong injection volume. Outlier samples are removed before normalization (4 here). With the processing option *Non-calibration samples only*, calibration samples are never removed. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note} ## Internal standards not found in a sample The mean and SD of each IS are taken from its non-zero values, and a zero (the IS was not found in that sample) counts as an outlying IS: a sample that misses many IS is an outlier. After the outlier check, the remaining zeros of the IS are replaced, for the normalization only, by the mean of that IS in the same file type (`Sample`, `QC`, `Standard` or `Blank`), or by its mean in all samples when it has no value in that file type. The [processing history](reports-and-exports.qmd#processing-history) lists every replaced zero. ::: ## 3.4 Raw RSD% of the selected IS ::: {.cell} ::: The RSD% of the raw peak areas of one IS (here **Cotinine-13C-d3_IS**) within each QC group and each sample class, with the number of samples. The QC groups are replicates of the same material, so their RSD% shows the technical variation alone. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## 3.5 Distribution of the selected IS The raw peak areas of the selected IS by sample group (left) and along the injection order (right). Outlier samples are drawn as crosses. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip} - **The boxes should be at the same height** in all groups: the IS was added in the same amount everywhere. A group clearly higher or lower suggests a matrix effect in that group. - **Along the injection order**, the points should form a flat band. A slope or a jump (e.g. at a new batch) is instrument drift, which the normalization corrects. ::: ## 3.6 Volumetric internal standard The volumetric IS (`vIS`) is added to the final extract just before injection; its peak area shows how constant the injected volume was. The bars are its raw peak area in each sample along the injection order; the table gives its RSD% within groups of samples. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip} - **A flat row of bars** and a low RSD% mean a constant volume. Single low bars are samples with less volume (or a failed injection); the processing option *Pre-normalize by the volumetric IS* corrects for this. ::: ## 3.7 Internal standards over the sequence ::: {.cell} ::: The peak areas of all (non-failed) internal standards per sample along the injection order, stacked, with a LOESS trend of their total. The app has two panels to compare: here the raw values (top) and after the best normalization, Multivariate (PCA) (bottom). ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip} - **Raw**: the height of the stacks follows the instrument response; a trend in the LOESS line is drift over the run. - **Normalized**: the stacks should become even and the trend flat. If they do not, the normalization did not correct the drift well; compare the methods in 3.8. :::
